assumptions: Treating the mapped CVEs as the intended source and target is an inference, never a fact.
Inferring that the source's potential code execution could provide the target's local-user capability is an inference, never a fact.
Inferring that Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop are co-located on the same Windows host is an inference, never a fact.

evidence_quotes.quote: inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI
allows local users to write to arbitrary files
via vectors involving a hard link to a log file

missing_conditions: Victim visits or opens the attacker-controlled remote page required for CVE-2019-3562 applicability.
CVE-2019-3562's potential code execution actually occurs rather than only HTML injection or UI spoofing.
The resulting capability is execution or equivalent local-user activity on the relevant host.
Oculus Browser and the vulnerable Oculus Desktop installation are deployed on the same host.
The host runs Windows and a vulnerable Oculus Desktop version described by CVE-2020-1885.
A privileged OVRRedir.exe process is running and writes to the relevant log file.
The hard-link vector and required file-system permissions are available for the attempted exploitation.
The source capability can create the hard link or otherwise satisfy CVE-2020-1885's local-user prerequisite.
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 describes arbitrary HTML injection into the Oculus Browser UI and only says an attacker could "potentially execute code"; it does not establish actual code execution, local-user capability, operating system, or host placement. CVE-2020-1885 describes a Windows local-user issue in which a privileged OVRRedir.exe process can write to arbitrary files through a hard-link-to-log-file vector, but its vulnerable product, process state, file-system conditions, and local-user prerequisite are unverified. If the source's potential execution occurs as a local user on the same Windows host running the vulnerable Oculus Desktop process, it could provide a bounded capability bridge to the target prerequisite. Those conditions are not entailed by the supplied descriptions, so the edge is conditional and cannot enter a strict graph as established causality.
